# GPU Compute Market Brief — November 10, 2026

## Pricing Trends: Broad-Based Inflation, One Notable Exception

On-demand GPU pricing has climbed across nearly every tier over the past four quarters. The **B300** (288 GB VRAM, 2,250 TFLOPS FP16) now averages **$12.05/hr** on-demand, up from $8.11 two quarters ago (+49%). The **B200** sits at **$9.90/hr** (up from $7.51), and the **H200** at **$6.84/hr** (up from $5.12). Even commodity workloads feel the squeeze: the **A100-80GB** averages $3.08/hr (vs. $2.34 in Q3), and the **RTX-5090** has risen from $0.51 to $0.91/hr.

The standout exception is the **GB200**, which has *fallen* from $19.51 to **$15.58/hr** on-demand (−20%), with Vast.ai listing it at just $8.76/hr. This suggests early Blackwell Ultra supply is catching up to demand.

**Best FLOPS-per-dollar** right now: AMD **MI300X** at 379 FLOPS/$ (cheapest at $2.39/hr on RunPod), followed by MI325X (344) and B200 (263).

| **NVDA** | $178.67 | −4.3% | −5.4% | $164.27 – $243.37 |
| **AMD** | $508.58 | **+13.3%** | **+127.6%** | $188.22 – $658.52 |

AMD's outsized YTD gain (+128%) reflects MI300X/MI325X gaining real cloud traction, while NVDA trades 27% below its 52-week high amid export-control overhang.

- **Export controls tighten:** Nvidia is reportedly capping Chinese-customer data-center revenue at 49%, and Chinese lab Moonshot is routing Blackwell procurement through European data centers.
- **Power is the bottleneck, not silicon:** Amazon's $5 B in Nvidia AI servers reportedly sit idle in warehouses; Nvidia's Kyber racks demand power equivalent to ~500 homes.
- **Nvidia is underwriting $164.5 B** in AI data-center buildouts to sustain GPU sell-through, and has unveiled a "shipping-container AI factory" to compress deployment timelines.
- A prominent bear argues current scarcity is "created by Jensen Huang," not structural.

1. **Lock in H100/H200 now if you need them by Q1 2027.** Prediction markets imply H200 will fall to ~$1.75/hr by May 2027 and H100-SXM to ~$2.13/hr by January—but that assumes no further power-constrained supply shocks.
